what: This file gives UV, sunlight at the ground, clear-sky days and haze for each ranked square of the Mars part.
service: NASA POWER, POWER Climatology API v2.10.1, regional endpoint, community RE. Data set named in the answers: CERES SYN1deg (SYN1DEG; ALLSKY_KT and CLRSKY_DAYS: SYN1DEG and POWER).

squares.order: the order of squares.ids in site/data/mars.json (the page's Mars file)

monthly.how_to_read: square i, field k, month j (0 = January): the uint16 at byte offset 2 * ((i * 5 + k) * 12 + j)

yearly.how_to_read: square i, field k: the uint16 at byte offset 1558080 + 2 * (i * 8 + k)

layout.not_by_month: clear-sky sunlight, clearness and top-of-atmosphere sunlight are in the source as yearly values only

uv_index.what: ALLSKY_SFC_UV_INDEX by month: UV index averaged over all 24 hours of the day, night included
uv_index.what_it_is_not: Not the noon UV index of a weather forecast. It is the mean over all 24 hours of the month's mean day, night included. Checked: the 24 hourly values of the service's hour-based set average to it within 2 percent in most box-months. So it is several times lower than the brightest hour, which uv_index_brightest_hour gives.

uv_index_brightest_hour.what: By month, the highest of the 24 hourly values of the month's mean day, local solar time. From the service's hour-based set ALLSKY_SFC_UV_INDEX_HR. It is the figure closest to a forecast's noon UV index.
uv_index_brightest_hour.what_it_is_not: Not one day's noon value and not the clearest day's. It is the highest of the 24 hourly values of the month's mean day, all sky, for a 1 degree box. Hours are local solar time, as the service labels them. The service gives no definition of the hour-based set beyond its name.

sun_kwh_m2_day.what: ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN by month, kWh per m2 per day on level ground, all sky (January first)
sun_kwh_m2_day.what_it_is_not: Not the sunlight on a tilted panel or in one hour, and not a measurement at the square. It is the energy reaching level ground in a mean day of the month, night included. Satellite-based, under the real mix of cloud and clear, for a 1 degree box about 111 km tall.

clear_days.what: CLRSKY_DAYS by month divided by the years the count was summed over. Days a month with daytime cloud over the 1 degree box under 10 percent. Null if those years are not settled.
clear_days.what_it_is_not: Not the days a camera at the square sees a clear sky. A day counts only when daytime cloud over the whole 1 degree box is under 10 percent. So a partly cloudy box, or a coastal box with sea cloud, counts as not clear. The service sums the count over all years; it is divided here by the years the check found.

aod_550.what: AOD_55 by month: aerosol optical depth at 550 nm, all particles in the air column, dimensionless
aod_550.years_the_values_fit: 2001 to any end year from 2018 to 2021 (the check cannot tell them apart)
aod_550.what_it_is_not: This is not dust alone, and it is not dust on the ground. It is the optical depth at 550 nm of all fine particles in the air column together. These are dust, smoke, sea salt, haze and pollution, as a monthly mean for a 1 degree box.

sun_kwh_m2_day_year.what: ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, the service's annual value, kWh per m2 per day
sun_kwh_m2_day_year.what_it_is_not: Not the sunlight on a tilted panel or in one hour, and not a measurement at the square. It is the energy reaching level ground in a mean day of the month, night included. Satellite-based, under the real mix of cloud and clear, for a 1 degree box about 111 km tall.

sun_clear_sky_kwh_m2_day_year.what: CLRSKY_SFC_SW_DWN annual: sunlight on level ground were there no cloud, kWh/m2/day
sun_clear_sky_kwh_m2_day_year.what_it_is_not: This is not what reaches the ground on a typical day. It is what would reach a level surface on the same days if there were no cloud.

uv_index_year.what: ALLSKY_SFC_UV_INDEX, the service's annual value (24-hour mean)
uv_index_year.what_it_is_not: Not the noon UV index of a weather forecast. It is the mean over all 24 hours of the month's mean day, night included. Checked: the 24 hourly values of the service's hour-based set average to it within 2 percent in most box-months. So it is several times lower than the brightest hour, which uv_index_brightest_hour gives.

uv_index_brightest_hour_max.what_it_is_not: Not one day's noon value and not the clearest day's. It is the highest of the 24 hourly values of the month's mean day, all sky, for a 1 degree box. Hours are local solar time, as the service labels them. The service gives no definition of the hour-based set beyond its name.

clear_days_year.what: The service's annual CLRSKY_DAYS divided by the same years: such days a year. The service gives its fill value for the year whenever the total passes 1800. There the sum of its 12 months is used (counts.squares_with_clear_days_year_from_month_sum).
clear_days_year.what_it_is_not: Not the days a camera at the square sees a clear sky. A day counts only when daytime cloud over the whole 1 degree box is under 10 percent. So a partly cloudy box, or a coastal box with sea cloud, counts as not clear. The service sums the count over all years; it is divided here by the years the check found.

aod_550_year.years_the_values_fit: 2001 to any end year from 2018 to 2021 (the check cannot tell them apart)
aod_550_year.what_it_is_not: This is not dust alone, and it is not dust on the ground. It is the optical depth at 550 nm of all fine particles in the air column together. These are dust, smoke, sea salt, haze and pollution, as a monthly mean for a 1 degree box.

clearness_index_year.what: ALLSKY_KT annual: share of top-of-atmosphere sunlight that reaches the ground
clearness_index_year.what_it_is_not: This is not a share of clear days. It is the share of top-of-atmosphere sunlight that gets to level ground in a mean day, with cloud, haze and air together.

top_of_atmosphere_kwh_m2_day_year.what: TOA_SW_DWN annual: sunlight on a level surface above the atmosphere, kWh/m2/day
top_of_atmosphere_kwh_m2_day_year.what_it_is_not: This is not sunlight at the ground. It is what a level surface would get above the atmosphere. We keep it to compare the ground figures with it.

tag: NASA POWER, monthly mean on a coarse grid

rules.clear_days_rule: The service's CLRSKY_DAYS climatology is a count summed over all years of its period. Monthly values above 31 occur, such as 137 in January at 28.5 S 70.5 W. clear_days = that count / 20 years.
rules.uv_rule: The UV index (uv_index) is ALLSKY_SFC_UV_INDEX of the service. It is a mean over all 24 hours of the day, and it includes the night. The UV index of the brightest hour (uv_index_brightest_hour) is the highest hourly value of ALLSKY_SFC_UV_INDEX_HR for the mean day of each month.
rules.cell_to_grid: the 1 degree box that holds the square centre (twinfinder.cloud.grid_box); no square sits on a box edge
rules.null_rule: unknown is null, never 0: a parameter or block not fetched, a fill value (-999), or clear days whose years are not settled

clear_days_fallback: There is no fallback. The Mars source has no cloud amount, thus an unknown count of clear days stays unknown.

sunlight_top_of_atmosphere.what: sunlight at the top of the atmosphere
sunlight_top_of_atmosphere.source: NASA NSSDCA Mars Fact Sheet and Earth Fact Sheet (saved: data/raw/mars_climate/factsheets/)
sunlight_top_of_atmosphere.mars_range_how: 586.2 W/m2 times (227.956 / distance)^2 at aphelion 249.261 and perihelion 206.650 million km

dust_optical_depth.source: Mars: Martinez et al. 2017, Space Science Reviews, section 3.1 (saved: data/raw/mars_sites/martinez2017_ssr_review.pdf)
dust_optical_depth.note: Mars: the optical depth is usually below 1 in the aphelion season (Ls 0-180). It is above 3 at the peak of global dust storms (record of 7 landers on the surface). Dust is in the sky all year. Earth: the global mean optical depth at 550 nm is approximately 0.1-0.2. This Earth figure is from memory and is not checked.

uv_cut_off.unit: nm, the shortest wavelength of sunlight that reaches the ground
uv_cut_off.source: From the literature, not checked against a saved file in this run. Mars: Cockell et al. 2000, Icarus 146, 343-359. Earth: the ozone cut-off near 290 nm.
uv_cut_off.note: Mars has almost no ozone. Thus UV-C (200-280 nm) reaches the surface of Mars, but it never reaches the ground of Earth. On Mars, only CO2 stops light shorter than approximately 190-200 nm.

sunlight_at_the_ground.what: daily sunlight on level ground at a Mars site (kWh/m2 a day or W/m2)

uv_index.what: a UV index or UV irradiance at the ground of a Mars site

cloud_free_days.what: a count of cloud-free (or dust-free) days at a Mars site

dust_only_optical_depth_earth.what: a dust-only optical depth for Earth (the service offers none)

sentences.sunlight: Earth's sunniest ranked box (-23.5, -67.5, Altiplano and Puna) gets 7.37 kWh per m2 a day on level ground. It keeps 0.8 of the sunlight arriving above its air. Above its air Mars gets 586.2 W/m2, 0.431 of Earth's 1361.0. How much reaches the Mars ground is not in our data.
sentences.uv: Earth's highest UV index is 19.7 in the brightest hour of the mean day (-23.5, -67.5, Altiplano and Puna). As a 24-hour mean it is 3.38. No Earth place matches Mars in kind: sunlight down to 190 nm reaches the Mars ground, 290 nm on Earth. Source: literature, not checked against a saved file in this run: Cockell et al. 2000, Icarus 146, 343-359 (Mars); the ozone cut-off near 290 nm (Earth). A Mars UV index is not in our data.
sentences.clear_days: Earth's clearest ranked box (23.5, 27.5, Sahara) has 276 days a year with daytime cloud under 10 percent over the whole box. A count of clear days on Mars is not in our data. Our files say dust is in the Mars sky all year (Mars: Martinez et al. 2017, Space Science Reviews, section 3.1 (saved: data/raw/mars_sites/martinez2017_ssr_review.pdf)).
sentences.haze: Earth's ranked squares range in yearly aerosol optical depth from 0.00 (-84.5, -177.5, Transantarctic Mountains) to 0.72 (31.5, 102.5, Tibetan Plateau). North of 60 S the lowest is 0.02 (-50.5, -69.5, Patagonian Desert). The haziest month reaches 1.13 (31.5, 72.5). These are all particles together, not dust alone, rounded to two decimals. Our files give Mars dust optical depth generally below 1 in the aphelion season. At the peak of global dust storms it is above 3 (Mars: Martinez et al. 2017, Space Science Reviews, section 3.1 (saved: data/raw/mars_sites/martinez2017_ssr_review.pdf)). Earth's haziest month is just above that 'below 1', and far from a Mars dust storm.

mars_comparison.rule: Mars figures only as data/derived/mars_sites.json holds them (site cards made from mars_climate.json); 'not in our data' where they do not; nothing typed from memory

unknown: 65535 in mars_environment.bin and null here: never 0
